blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: A developer who has not seen the plan cannot answer "at what price is a price premium?": the rule is hidden in `(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8`, a shift and a bitmask with a magic hex value, which reads as a threshold but is not one (for example 128 cents gives 8 & 1000 = 8, "hi", while 256 cents gives 16 & 1000 = 0, "lo" — the grouping is not monotonic in price). The comma operator, `||=` inside an index expression and the reduce accumulator fold all of this into one line, and the names `bucket`, `ps`, `a`, `p`, "hi"/"lo" and the `Record<string, Price[]>` return type do not match the doc comment's "cheap and premium". Rewrite it as a named function with a named constant for the threshold (e.g. `PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`), a plain comparison (`p.cents >= PREMIUM_THRESHOLD_CENTS`), a loop or two `filter` calls, and an explicit return type such as `{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }`; if the bit arithmetic is intended, a comment must say why — otherwise the developer should check the rule against the spec, since the shape hides what it computes.
findings.title: `bucket` packs an unexplained bitmask threshold into a dense one-liner
